name: Private credit stress
value: BDCs at steep NAV discounts; no forced sales
summary: Several listed BDCs trade at steep discounts to NAV and are merging; no forced asset sales or bank losses found
state: Reuters reported on 13 Nov that several listed business development companies trade at steep discounts to reported NAV; Investcorp's BDC closed at 61 cents on 9 Nov before agreeing a takeover at 90% of adjusted NAV, and the buyer's NAV per share fell 9.4% in the quarter to September. Large semi-liquid funds have capped redemptions repeatedly this year. Searches on 13 Nov found no simultaneous wave of gates, forced asset sales or losses spreading to banks or insurers, so Watch holds.
for_you: Exposure sits mainly with investors in semi-liquid private credit funds and listed BDCs, where withdrawals can be limited and share prices can sit well below reported asset values. Mid-sized companies that borrow from these lenders can face tighter terms.
rubric_hit: Watch: listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV and large funds limit redemptions; no simultaneous gates or forced sales (Alert)

sources.title: Reuters (via 104.9 The Wolf) — Private credit roundup: Lenders consolidate, seek scale as earnings pressure builds

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
